title: Confidence Ribbon: Explainable Token-Economy Microinteractions for Cache & Batch
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Operators configuring batching and caching often cannot predict the downstream cost/latency/quality trade-offs of a change. The Console needs a compact, scannable UI element that explains the token-economy impact of presets and per-route tweaks and surfaces risk signals during rollouts.

Goal: Design a "Confidence Ribbon" — a horizontal micro-visualization and interaction surface that sits on the batch/cache config card (and in rollout diffs). It should: 1) show predicted cost delta, latency percentile shift, and quality-confidence band for a given preset; 2) allow quick staging of presets (staged ramp: 5/25/100) with templated microcopy; 3) expose guardrails (max token multiplier, do-not-prefetch patterns) and one-click rollback; 4) provide hover explainers and an optional deep link to a simulation sandbox.

Scope: High-fidelity prototype of the ribbon and the staged-presets microflow, microcopy for tooltips, handoff tokens for engineering telemetry fields, and an accessibility pass on the micro-interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Ribbon mockups for default / canary / degraded states in Figma with copy and token values
Hover explainers for each metric (cost, latency, quality/confidence) with simple math and example calculation
Microflow for staged rollout (3-step ramp) annotated with required backend flags and event names
Guardrail panel design that allows toggling 'prevent-prefetch-for-sensitive-routes' and setting a max token multiplier
Design tokens and interaction specs exported for engineering handoff (hover states, aria labels, colors, spacing)
decisions: Show three channels in ribbon: cost delta (USD per 1k tokens), latency p95 change (ms), quality-confidence band (± BLEU-like proxy).
Use compact sparkline + colored band to indicate confidence rather than raw score to avoid overfitting expectations.
Staged rollout default steps: 5% -> 25% -> 100% (configurable by eng via rollout API).
Prefetch will not run for routes labeled with 'sensitive' unless user explicitly disables the guardrail.
Expose a 'simulate' deep-link that opens the Console sandbox with the current preset applied to a sample workload.
tradeoffs: Surface simplified quality metric to avoid presenting noisy absolute scores — tradeoff: less granular than model evals but more understandable to operators.
Keeping the ribbon compact limits how many knobs we can show inline; advanced options move to the guardrail panel — tradeoff: discoverability vs clutter.
Default staged rollout values are conservative to reduce customer risk but add latency to getting to full savings — tradeoff: safety vs speed of cost reduction.
reviewers_feedback: PM (Lina Gomez): "Love the confidence band idea. Please add a short example showing how cost savings accumulates across staged steps (5% -> 25% -> 100%)."

Eng (Ravi Singh): "Instrumentation is required: we need event names + params for every staged step and a telemetry contract (ENG-24198). Also concerned about computing quality proxy in realtime—prefer precomputed estimates surfaced by runtime."
Security (Olivia Martinez): "Add an explicit guardrail toggle for PII-sensitive routes and document behavioral expectations when disabled."
Design lead (Hana Ito): "Simplify microcopy for tooltips — avoid domain jargon. Provide 1-line action affordances (e.g., 'Simulate', 'Stage', 'Rollback')."
